title: Add a Windows DNS/DHCP Server to Micetro

cta.text: See Micetro with your Microsoft servers

prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "Add a Windows DNS/DHCP Server to Micetro".
Story: Bring a Windows DNS and DHCP Server Under Micetro, Without an Agent
A new domain controller is already serving DNS and DHCP. Watch BlueCat Micetro add both services in two short wizards with nothing installed on the server, and pick up the scope that was already there.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
17 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element:
1. Two domain controllers, DLG-DC01 and DLG-DC02, are managed here today, each as a DNS service and a DHCP service. A third, DLG-DC03, is already running DNS and DHCP and has not been added to Micetro yet. Select Add service to bring it in.
2. Services are added one type at a time, and DHCP and DNS are separate, so start with Microsoft DHCP. Continue to its properties, where you name the server.
3. Agentless: nothing is installed on DC03. Micetro connects from the Central host with its service account, so there is nothing to deploy and no password to enter. Add DC03 by its fully qualified name, then continue to the summary.
4. Review the service type and the server name before anything is written. Select Add.
5. Micetro asks for a change comment on every write, so each change has a reason on record. Add a short one, then save.
6. The DHCP service is added and its first synchronization has started. DNS on the same server is a separate service, so add it the same way.
7. DNS is its own service, so add it the same way. Microsoft DNS is selected; continue to its properties.
8. Agentless again: the same Central host and service account manage DNS, and nothing goes on DC03. Enter the same fully qualified name, then continue to the summary.
9. The summary shows a Microsoft DNS service on DC03, reached through the Central host. Select Add.
10. Another change comment, because this is another write. Add one, then save.
11. DNS is added too. Open the service list to see DC03 next to the other controllers.
12. DLG-DC03 now appears as a DNS service and a DHCP service on 192.168.2.55, state OK, next to DC01 and DC02. Its scope is not in Micetro yet, so pull it in: open the row menu on the DHCP service.
13. The row menu lists everything you can do with the server. Choose Synchronize to read what is already on DC03.
14. Micetro confirms before it reads the server. Confirm.
15. The synchronization runs. When it finishes, the scope that was already configured on DC03 is in Micetro. Open the DHCP scopes list to find it.
16. Every DHCP scope Micetro knows about is in this one tree. Filter it to DC03's subnet.
17. There it is: the 192.168.2.0/24 scope that was already on DC03, with DLG-DC03 as its authority. Nothing was imported or rebuilt, and DC03 is ready for everything that follows.
Close: Both services added, nothing installed, and the existing scope is already in Micetro.
End with a call to action: See Micetro with your Microsoft servers.
